newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: FOCUS-Global rubber body raises reference price.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Global rubber body raises reference price.

text.p: The International Natural Rubber Organisation (INRO) on Friday announced a higher reference price for its buffer stock at the end of its first meeting under a new global rubber pact.

INRO also announced the appointment of new key officials at the meeting, the first since the third International Natural Rubber Agreement (INRA 3) came into force last month after a year of tough negotiations.
"There was no issue...everything was agreed on," an INRO official told Reuters after the five-day council meeting.

INRA 3 is the world's only remaining global commodity agreement with economic provisions and a buffer stock that allows the industry to buy and sell rubber to stabilise prices. Two cycles of the agreement -- INRA 1 and INRA 2 -- have been completed under the administration of INRO.

James Hegarty, who was re-appointed buffer stock manager for another four-year term, said INRO decided to raise its buffer stock reference price by four percent to reflect the increase in world rubber prices.
The reference price is basically a neutral level where INRO's buffer stock manager does not intervene to buy or sell rubber in the market.
The new reference price has been raised to 214.95 Malaysian/Singapore cents a kg from 206.68 cents previously.
The price is calculated as a weighted average of the Singapore and Malaysian currencies.

"The old reference price is not valid any more as the market price of rubber has been higher throughout the year," Hegarty told Reuters. Malaysian rubber is currently trading at an average of 300 cents a kg.
Hegarty said the "may sell" and "must sell" prices for the buffer stock manager were 247 and 258 cents a kg, respectively.
The "may buy" and "must buy" prices were 183 and 172 cents, respectively, he said.
In a statement after the meeting, INRO announced that Malaysia's Ahmad Zubeir Noordin had been appointed executive director of INRO to fill the top job held previously by Thailand's Pong Sono.

Zubeir has been working in the Malaysian commodities arena for more than 25 years. Malaysia fought hard to get that post after Indonesia put in a strong claim and at one point threated to pull out of the agreement.
The statement said Gerard Loyen of France was the new deputy executive director.
INRO said that 97 percent of rubber exporters and 82 percent of importers had now ratified INRA 3. China was the last entrant to the pact.
INRO said in the statement it had pushed back the deadline for all rubber producing and consuming countries to ratify the agreement to December 31, 1997 from January 1 of this year.
